[[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] in blue, [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] in red, [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] in yellow and [[Merton Park Ward Residents Association]] in white. }} '''Elections for the [[London Borough of Merton]]''' were held on 5 May 2022 to elect all 57 members of [[Merton London Borough Council]] in England. The elections took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]]. The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, which reduced the number of councillors from 60 to 57. [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] remained the largest party following the election, winning 31 seats. For the first time in the council's history, the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] became the largest opposition party, winning 17 seats. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]], previously the largest opposition party, won seven seats. == Background == {{See also|Merton London Borough Council#History}}Since its formation, Merton has variously been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control, [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control and [[no overall control]]. In the [[2018 Merton London Borough Council election|previous council election in 2018]], Labour and the Conservatives lost seats to the Liberal Democrats. Labour won 34 seats with 46.9% of the vote across the borough, while the Conservatives won 17 seats with 31.5% of the vote. The Liberal Democrats rose to six seats with 14.6% of the vote and the Merton Park Ward Independent Residents continued to hold three seats with 3.3% of the vote across the borough.{{Cite |language=en}} A by-election to fill the seat was held in June 2019, which was won by the Liberal Democrat candidate Jenifer Gould.{{Cite web|last=Baston|first=Lewis|date=2019-06-21|title=Merton: Lib Dem gain in Cannon Hill by-election is blow for Labour and worrying for local Tory MP|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/merton-lib-dem-gain-in-cannon-hill-by-election-is-blow-for-labour-and-worrying-for-local-tory-mp/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}} One of the Liberal Democrat councillors for West Barnes, Carl Quilliam who had previously lost the contest to become the Liberal Democrat Parliamentary Candidate for Wimbledon in 2019, defected to the Labour Party in June 2020 citing the national leadership of [[Keir Starmer]].{{Cite web|last=O'Connor|first=Tara|date=2020-06-16|title=Merton Lib Dem councillor joins Labour|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/south-london-news/merton-lib-dem-councillor-joins-18426359|access-date=2021-10-20|website=MyLondon|language=en}} In March 2021, Kelly Braund, a Labour councillor for St Helier, resigned because she was moving to Scotland.{{Cite web|last=O'Connor|first=Tara|date=2021-03-11|title=A Merton councillor has resigned prompting a by-election|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/south-london-news/merton-councillor-resigned-prompting-election-20086880|access-date=2021-10-20|website=MyLondon|language=en}} At the subsequent by-election, the seat was held for Labour by Helen Dollimore.{{Cite web|date=2021-05-08|title=London Elections 2021 Day Two: By-election round-up|url=https://www.swlondoner.co.uk/news/08052021-london-elections-2021-day-2-by-election-round-up/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=South West Londoner|language=en-GB}} The Labour councillor Mark Allison succeeded Stephen Alambritis as leader of the council in November 2020.{{Cite web|date=2020-11-20|title=Mark Allison is named new leader of Merton council – and his cabinet is most diverse in borough's history|url=https://londonnewsonline.co.uk/mark-allison-is-named-new-leader-of-merton-council-and-his-cabinet-is-most-diverse-in-boroughs-history/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120120028/https://londonnewsonline.co.uk/mark-allison-is-named-new-leader-of-merton-council-and-his-cabinet-is-most-diverse-in-boroughs-history/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=20 November 2020|access-date=2021-10-20|website=South London News|language=en-GB}} Along with most other London boroughs, Merton was subject to a boundary review ahead of the 2022 election. The [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]] concluded that the council should have 57 seats, falling from the previous 60 seats, and produced new election boundaries following a period of consultation.{{Cite web|title=LGBCE {{!}} Merton {{!}} LGBCE Site|url=http://www.lgbce.org.uk/all-reviews/greater-london/greater-london/merton|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.lgbce.org.uk|language=en}} == Electoral process == Merton, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected. All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election. ==Results== {{Election summary begin|title = 2022 Merton London Borough Council election}} {{Election summary party| |party = Labour Party (UK) |seats = '''31''' |gain = |loss = |net = {{decrease}} 3 |seats % =54.4 |votes % = 42.3 |votes = 70,423 |plus/minus = -4.6 }} {{Election summary party| |party = Liberal Democrats (UK) |seats = '''17''' |gain = |loss = |net = {{increase}} 11 |seats % =29.8 |votes % = 25.0 |votes = 41,655 |plus/minus = +10.4 }} {{Election summary party| |party = Conservative Party (UK) |seats = '''7''' |gain = |loss = |net = {{decrease}} 10 |seats % =12.3 |votes % = 26.1 |votes = 43,382 |plus/minus = -5.4 }} {{Election summary party| |party = Merton Park Ward Residents Association |seats = '''2''' |gain = |loss = |net = {{decrease}} 1 |seats % =3.5 |votes % = 2.1 |votes = 3,576 |plus/minus = -1.2 }} {{Election summary party| |party = Green Party of England and Wales |seats = '''0''' |gain = 0 |loss = 0 |net = {{steady}} |seats % =0.0 |votes % = 4.3 |votes = 7,161 |plus/minus = +1.5 }} {{Election summary party| |party = Trade Unionist and Socialist Coalition |seats = '''0''' |gain = 0 |loss = 0 |net = {{steady}} |seats % =0.0 |votes % = 0.1 |votes = 154 |plus/minus = +0.1 }} {{Election box end}} Due to the boundary changes, which reduced the number of seats from 60 to 57, reporting the gains/losses by party is not straightforward. The BBC used a calculation which takes into account the changes relative to the expected previous result under the new boundaries. These give: Labour -4, Liberal Democrats +12, Conservatives -8, Merton Park Independents: no change.{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2022/england/councils/E09000024 | title=Merton result - Local Elections 2022 | work=BBC News }} === Council composition === File:Merton London Borough Council 2018 apportionment.svg|{{centre|Council composition after the 2018 election and before the 2022 election}} File:United Kingdom Merton Council Council 2022.png|{{centre|Council composition after the 2022 election}} {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2018 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2022 election ! colspan="3" |After 2022 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
